summary: Loudeil Seed Holdings, LLC (client, Buyer) acquired the vegetable seed genetics business of Naitox Vegetable Genetics, Inc. (Seller) under an Asset Purchase Agreement signed February 9, 2026. Closing occurred March 2, 2026. The purchase price was $48,500,000: $40,000,000 in cash and an $8,500,000 Seller Note issued by Loudeil. The assets include hybrid tomato and pepper germplasm, parent and inbred lines, breeding records, the TY-Shield marker panel for Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus resistance, and seed inventory. Loudeil also hired Naitox's Head of Vegetable Breeding, Dr. Ilse Varnholt. The folder holds nine documents: the APA, the Seller Note, a post-closing side letter dated April 28, 2026, the Bill of Sale and Assumption, Dr. Varnholt's Key Employee Agreement, the IP Assignment Agreement, the Disclosure Schedule, a pre-signing mutual NDA, and a landlord estoppel certificate for the Salinas breeding station. The partner wants a memo on issues that expose Loudeil. Six issues are planted: (1) the noteholder may freely transfer the Seller Note, together with its information rights; (2) the Inventory Dispute Notice was delivered after the APA window; (3) the general rep survival period ends before the purity rep can be tested; (4) the IP Assignment Agreement, through the APA precedence clause, pulls the IP title reps out of the Fundamental Representations carve-out; (5) the Key Employee Agreement treats as Dr. Varnholt's property inventions that the APA conveys as Pre-Closing Inventions; (6) the side letter adds an uncapped Buyer indemnity for transition grower orders.

parties.name: Loudeil Seed Holdings, LLC
parties.role: Buyer under the APA; maker of the Seller Note; employer under the Key Employee Agreement; the firm's client

parties.name: Naitox Vegetable Genetics, Inc.
parties.role: Seller under the APA; holder of the Seller Note; assignor under the IP Assignment Agreement

parties.name: Dr. Ilse Varnholt
parties.role: Seller's former Head of Vegetable Breeding; key employee hired by Buyer at Closing

facts.value: $48,500,000, of which $8,500,000 is paid by the Seller Note
APA prevails over Ancillary Agreements, except IP Assignment Agreement controls on Transferred IP conveyance and representations

issues.label: unrestricted assignment
issues.description: Section 10.2 of the Seller Note lets the Holder sell, assign or transfer the Note, in whole or in part, to any person, with no consent from the Maker (Loudeil) and no notice to it. Two other provisions of the Note pass to any transferee. Section 7.1 requires Loudeil to deliver to 'the Holder' quarterly reports of seed sales by variety and the status of its breeding pipeline. Section 8.2 lets 'the Holder' accelerate the Note on a reporting default. Read together, these let Naitox move the Note, and with it Loudeil's commercially sensitive breeding and sales data, to a competing seed company or a distressed-debt buyer, which could then use the acceleration right as leverage. The APA's assignment clause (Section 11.4) covers only the APA itself and does not reach the Note.
detect_terms: without the consent of the Maker
issues.expected_finding: The Seller Note lets Naitox transfer the Note to any person, including a competitor, without Loudeil's consent, and the transferee would receive the Section 7.1 sales and breeding-pipeline reports and the acceleration right. Loudeil should seek an amendment requiring its consent to transfers, barring transfers to competitors, and limiting or confidentiality-protecting the information covenant.

issues.label: expired notice window
issues.description: Section 2.4(b) of the APA requires Buyer to deliver any Inventory Dispute Notice objecting to Seller's Closing Seed Inventory Statement within 45 days after the Closing Date. Otherwise the statement becomes final and binding. The Bill of Sale (D4) fixes the Closing Date as March 2, 2026, so the deadline was April 16, 2026. The side letter dated April 28, 2026 (D3, Section 4) records that Buyer delivered its Inventory Dispute Notice on April 24, 2026, eight days late. It also records that Buyer maintains the notice is valid and that both parties reserve their rights. Neither document alone shows the lapse. The APA states the window but not the delivery date, and the side letter states the delivery date and Buyer's position but not the window. Loudeil has not accepted the Closing Seed Inventory Statement.
detect_terms: within 45 days after the Closing Date
issues.expected_finding: Loudeil's Inventory Dispute Notice, delivered April 24, 2026, missed the APA Section 2.4(b) deadline of April 16, 2026 (45 days after the March 2, 2026 Closing Date). Naitox can therefore argue that the Closing Seed Inventory Statement is final and binding. Because the April 28, 2026 side letter preserves Loudeil's objection and reserves rights, Loudeil should press waiver or estoppel arguments, or negotiate a written extension, and should assess whether the inventory shortfall can be pursued as an indemnity claim instead.
detect_terms2: delivered its Inventory Dispute Notice on April 24, 2026

issues.label: indemnity survival gap
issues.description: APA Section 4.11 has Seller represent that the germplasm and seed inventory meet a genetic purity of at least 98% and the stated disease-resistance traits, 'as determined by a grow-out trial conducted over a full growing season'. Section 9.1 provides that all representations other than Fundamental Representations survive only until 9 months after the Closing Date. Section 9.4 bars any claim not noticed with reasonable specificity before the survival period expires. Using the March 2, 2026 Closing Date stated in the Bill of Sale, the survival period ends December 2, 2026. The testing method that Section 4.11 itself prescribes needs a full field season plus analysis, so a breach could not practically be identified and documented with the required specificity before the claim window closes. Read together, these provisions make the core purity and trait representation close to unenforceable.
detect_terms: grow-out trial conducted over a full growing season
issues.expected_finding: The 9-month survival period in APA Section 9.1 ends December 2, 2026, before a grow-out trial of the kind Section 4.11 requires can establish a purity or trait breach. Loudeil's main protection on germplasm quality is therefore largely illusory. Loudeil should seek an amendment extending survival of Section 4.11 to at least 24 months, or should immediately serve a protective claim notice under Section 9.4.

issues.label: liability cap carve-out conflict
issues.description: The APA defines Fundamental Representations (Section 1.1) to include Section 4.9, Seller's title to Transferred IP. Section 9.6(b) excludes Fundamental Representations from the 12% Seller cap, and Section 9.1 gives them longer survival. Section 3.6 of the IP Assignment Agreement (D6) provides that its Section 3 representations are Assignor's sole representations concerning the Assigned IP and supersede Section 4.9 of the Purchase Agreement. On its own that reads as a routine integration of fuller IP reps. However, APA Section 11.9, the precedence clause, makes the IP Assignment Agreement control on representations concerning Transferred IP. Read together, the IP title reps now sit in the IP Assignment Agreement rather than APA Section 4.9. They are therefore no longer Fundamental Representations, fall under the 12% cap, and lose the carve-out. Title failure on the germplasm, the core asset, is now capped at a fraction of the price.
detect_terms: sole representations concerning the Assigned IP
supersede Section 4.9 of the Purchase Agreement
issues.expected_finding: Because APA Section 11.9 lets the IP Assignment Agreement control on Transferred IP representations, Section 3.6 of the IP Assignment Agreement replaces APA Section 4.9. The IP title representations therefore drop out of the Fundamental Representations carve-out in APA Section 9.6(b), so title claims to the germplasm are subject to the 12% cap and the shorter general survival. Loudeil should seek an amendment expressly treating the IP Assignment Agreement's title reps as Fundamental Representations.
detect_terms2: controls with respect to the conveyance of, and representations concerning, the Transferred IP

issues.label: defined term inconsistency
issues.description: APA Section 1.1 defines 'Pre-Closing Inventions' as all inventions, marker panels and breeding methods conceived by Seller or its Personnel before the Closing Date that relate to the Business. Section 2.1(c) conveys them to Buyer as Transferred Assets, and the Disclosure Schedule lists the TY-Shield marker panel among Seller-owned IP. Section 5.2 of the Key Employee Agreement (D5), which Loudeil itself signed with Dr. Varnholt, defines 'Prior Inventions' as inventions she conceived before her Employment Start Date (the Closing Date). It provides that they 'shall remain the sole property of Employee', and its Exhibit A lists the TY-Shield marker panel. Each clause alone is ordinary drafting. Read together, the same inventions are treated as a conveyed asset in one document and as the employee's personal property in another, and Loudeil has acknowledged her ownership in writing. The APA precedence clause (Section 11.9) does not resolve this, because the Key Employee Agreement is between Buyer and the employee and is not an Ancillary Agreement with Seller.
detect_terms: shall remain the sole property of Employee
issues.expected_finding: The Key Employee Agreement's definition of 'Prior Inventions' carves out pre-closing work, including the TY-Shield marker panel, as Dr. Varnholt's property, contradicting the APA's conveyance of 'Pre-Closing Inventions' as Transferred Assets. As a result, Loudeil's title to key trait IP is clouded, and its own acknowledgment undercuts a claim against Naitox. Loudeil should obtain a confirmatory assignment from Dr. Varnholt and amend Exhibit A to remove Business-related inventions.
detect_terms2: conceived by Seller or its Personnel prior to the Closing Date

issues.label: uncapped indemnity
issues.description: Section 3 of the April 28, 2026 side letter (D3) has Naitox fill pre-closing grower orders through June 30, 2026 ('Transition Orders') using seed produced by Loudeil. In Section 3.3, Buyer agrees to indemnify Seller for all Losses, including grower crop losses, arising from seed supplied for Transition Orders. Section 3.3 states that this indemnity is in addition to, and not subject to, any limitation in Article IX of the Purchase Agreement. APA Section 9.6(c) caps Buyer's liability only for claims under Section 9.3(a), so no cap reaches this obligation. In vegetable seed, grower crop-loss claims can far exceed the value of the seed, leaving Loudeil with unlimited exposure on a transition accommodation.
detect_terms: not subject to any limitation in Article IX
issues.expected_finding: Side letter Section 3.3 gives Naitox an uncapped indemnity from Loudeil for all Losses, including grower crop losses, on Transition Orders, outside the APA Article IX cap. Loudeil should seek a cap (for example, the price of the seed supplied), an exclusion of consequential and crop losses, and a carve-back for Losses caused by Naitox's own handling.
